claim: Core-lib wave-rollout mechanics, measured as a bun-vs-pnpm head-to-head. bun remains the recommended driver for its native mechanics (committed-bunfig frozen, package.json catalogs). Install speed, derived from bench/install-bench.json + bench/container-install-bench.json (see speedContext): of bun 1.3.14 and the two pnpm 12.8.1 linkers the fastest cold install is bun at 200 apps (the faster pnpm linker ×1.6 slower), pnpm-hoisted at 1,000 and 2,000 apps (bun ×3.1 slower and bun ×3.4 slower); truly-cold at 200 apps bun 1.3s vs pnpm-hoisted 2.2s (pnpm-hoisted ×1.7 slower); on the fresh CI frozen container (bun 1.3.14, pnpm 12.8.1) bun 0.93s vs pnpm 1.03s (pnpm ×1.1 slower). Determinism is the lockfile + a frozen install (the range is inert): bun fails closed on drift with one committed bunfig line (frozenLockfile=true); pnpm fails closed with --frozen-lockfile and auto-enables frozen in CI. Named catalogs route two cohorts to two versions in one lockfile and a repoint edits zero consumer manifests on both (bun in package.json, pnpm in pnpm-workspace.yaml). Both accept workspace: as a catalog value and link the local package (pnpm 12 lifted pnpm 10's ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_INVALID_WORKSPACE_SPEC rejection — parity). Both bake a CONCRETE range on publish (workspace:^ -> ^2.5.0), so advancing a universal lib is a republish-fanout. bun does not read pnpm-workspace.yaml catalogs, so author them in package.json.

speedContext.note: Derived from the cited records by scripts/_install-speed-context.mjs; which tool is faster depends on the scale and the install state, and every direction is stated (bench/install-bench.json: pnpm 12.8.1, bun 1.3.14, single-sample cells; "fastest" is among the three listed configurations). COLD install (no lockfile, fresh node_modules, warm store), bun / pnpm-isolated / pnpm-hoisted: 200 apps 0.28s / 0.43s / 0.46s — bun fastest, pnpm-isolated ×1.6 slower, pnpm-hoisted ×1.7 slower; 1,000 apps 2.9s / 2.1s / 0.96s — pnpm-hoisted fastest, bun ×3.1 slower, pnpm-isolated ×2.2 slower; 2,000 apps 8.6s / 6.8s / 2.5s — pnpm-hoisted fastest, bun ×3.4 slower, pnpm-isolated ×2.7 slower (bun is the slowest of the 5 measured configurations, both yarn linkers included). WARM (lockfile + store, node_modules removed), same order: 200 apps 0.27s / 0.25s / 0.26s — pnpm-isolated fastest, bun ×1.1 slower, pnpm-hoisted +3% vs fastest; 1,000 apps 2.8s / 2.5s / 0.59s — pnpm-hoisted fastest, bun ×4.8 slower, pnpm-isolated ×4.3 slower; 2,000 apps 8.8s / 7.3s / 1.1s — pnpm-hoisted fastest, bun ×8.3 slower, pnpm-isolated ×6.8 slower (bun is the slowest of the 5 measured configurations, both yarn linkers included). TRULY-COLD (fresh store + metadata, network) at 200 apps: bun 1.3s vs pnpm-hoisted 2.2s (pnpm-hoisted ×1.7 slower). CI-runner frozen install in a fresh container (bench/container-install-bench.json: pnpm 12.8.1, bun 1.3.14, 1,000 apps, medians of 5): fresh runner bun 0.93s vs pnpm 1.03s (pnpm ×1.1 slower); cache-restored bun 0.42s vs pnpm 0.50s (pnpm ×1.2 slower). Measured ceiling 2,000 apps.

bun.config: bunfig.toml [install] frozenLockfile=true; bare bun install on drift
bun.diagnostic: lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen
bun.sourceNote: frozen_lockfile is set only by --frozen-lockfile / `bun ci` / --production / bunfig (CommandLineArguments.zig:797, PackageManagerOptions.zig:335-344,613-620); env.isCI() only disables the progress bar (PackageManagerOptions.zig:392).

lockfilePortability.note: pnpm 12.8.1's launcher records the packageManager pin in pnpm-lock.yaml as a two-document YAML stream (packageManagerDependencies preamble document, measured present); with the pin removed a frozen install exits 1 (ERR_PNPM_BROKEN_LOCKFILE) — keep the pin with the lockfile through a rollout.

pnpm.note: pnpm 12.8.1 accepts every workspace: form as a catalog value and links the local package (sentinel-proved) — parity with bun; pnpm 10 rejected every form with ERR_PNPM_CATALOG_ENTRY_INVALID_WORKSPACE_SPEC

publishBakesConcrete.implication: a consumer catalog cannot repoint a baked range inside a dependent lib's tarball; a universal lib re-exported through every other lib advances by republishing its dependents.
